newsitem.title: USA: Seaream's MCA buys talk show syndicator.
newsitem.headline: Seaream's MCA buys talk show syndicator.

text.p: MCA Inc said its Television Group on Monday agreed to acquire substantially all assets of talk show syndicator Multimedia Entertainment, the force behind such popular series as "Sally Jessy Raphael" and "Jerry Springer," from Gannett Co Inc.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but industry sources said MCA paid less than $50 million for the assets.
MCA is 80 percent-owned by Seagram Co Ltd.
MCA also said Sally Jessy Raphael, host of the longest-running talk show in syndication, had agreed to extend her contract into the next millennium.

In addition to "Sally" and "Jerry," MCA will acquire the talk show "Pat Bullard" and distribution rights to "Crook & Chase," as well as library rights to "Donahue," the long-running talk show that helped popularize the talk show format for syndication.
As part of the deal, MCA will take over a slate of highly rated international talk shows produced locally in Britain, Germany, the Netherlands, France and Israel.
"The acquisition of Multimedia Entertainment instantly makes MCA TV a powerhouse in the critical domestic strip syndication business," MCA TV Group Chairman Greg Meidel said.
"As recent multi-year renewals indicate, stations recognize the strength of both 'Sally' and 'Jerry,'" he said.

"Sally Jessy Raphael," which began airing in 1982, appears in 147 markets covering 92 percent of the U.S. "Jerry," cleared in 113 markets with 82 percent coverage, is ranked ninth nationally among all talk shows.

The recently unveiled "Pat Bullard" is cleared in 126 markets covering 82 percent of the country. "Crook & Chase," a slow roll-out five-day-a-week talk show, has clearances in 85 markets covering 33 percent of the U.S.
